facts.text: Lakeview sits on the forested shores of Bull Shoals Lake, a 45,150‑acre man‑made reservoir built by the U.S. Corps of Engineers.
The town grew after the Bull Shoals Dam was finished in 1951, which flooded the upstream valley and created the lake.
Lakeview was originally called Trimble Flat, named for the Trimble family who settled the fertile plateau overlooking the White River in the 1880s.
Anglers flock to Lakeview each year for trout fishing on the White River and boating on Bull Shoals Lake.
The city’s marina has been expanded to provide access to thousands of miles of pristine water, supporting a thriving boating community.
Every fall, Lakeview’s trees burst into color, drawing day trippers on scenic drives through the Ozark Hills.
